fix_hint: Before the ~/.config/gh fallback, when process.platform === 'win32' and env.AppData (or APPDATA) is set, use path.join(AppData, 'GitHub CLI'). Mirror the header comment and add a test that injects the platform or the dir list.

title: --result turns scrub's fail-closed incomplete scan into a non-blocking pass, so an oversized file can carry a secret through the gate
detail: incompleteNoHits treats ANY scrub result with hit_count 0 and a non-empty not_scanned (or complete false) as 'could not judge' infrastructure, whatever the not_scanned reason. scrub lists product content there too: a file larger than --max-file-bytes (default 32 MiB), everything past the 2 GiB total, and a tracked path that is not a regular file in --worktree mode. scrub exits 2 on these precisely to fail closed, because the unscanned bytes may hold a secret. Confirmed: a repo whose creds.txt holds AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP plus padding, with pattern AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}; `scrub --max-file-bytes 100` exits 2 with hit_count 0 and not_scanned [{creds.txt, 'larger than 100 bytes'}]; `exit-codes blocks 2 --verb scrub --result out.json` returns class infrastructure, blocks false. The same file scanned in full is a hit (regression). With the default cap, padding a secret-bearing file past 32 MiB does the same, and push-gate takes the same path via line 97 (scrub.ran true, hit_count 0, incomplete). A PR author controls file size, so CI wired to --result lets a secret through. The r3 fix only needed the partial-clone / unreachable-remote case.
fix_hint: Only reclassify when every not_scanned entry has an environment reason (e.g. 'object not available locally (partial clone?)'); keep 'larger than N bytes', 'total size limit reached', 'not a regular file on disk' and any unknown reason as a blocking regression. Add tests for an oversized-file result for scrub and push-gate that assert blocks true.

title: Packaged push-gate test never checks the egress log
detail: Only the first packaged test asserts pkg.egress() is empty (line 32). The second test runs a real push-gate check plus four exit-codes calls under the no-egress preload, and never reads the log. The preload refuses network attempts by throwing, and push-gate turns a thrown error into 'could not run' with exit 2 and scrub.ran false, which is exactly what this test expects. So an egress attempt in that path would be refused, hidden by the expected outcome, and pass, which weakens the egress_zero finish line for this check. A manual probe found no egress today.
fix_hint: Add assert.deepEqual(pkg.egress(), []) at the end of the second packaged test.

title: trouble-log quietly skips redaction when git is missing or rev-parse fails
detail: loadSecrets catches every error from secretsRoots, including 'cannot run git' (git not installed) and 'git rev-parse failed' (for example git's 'dubious ownership' refusal in a container or CI checkout with a mounted repo). It then falls back to [cwd]. The secrets file is git-ignored and usually exists only in the main checkout, so a run from a linked worktree or a subfolder finds no secrets. The verb then exits 0 with secrets=[] and prints the raw text. Confirmed: main checkout with .claude/kit/secrets = 'SuperSecretToken123', run from a linked worktree. With git on PATH the output is 'failed: Login - bad [REDACTED]'. With git removed from PATH, or with GIT_DIR=/nonexistent, it is 'failed: Login - bad SuperSecretToken123', exit 0. In the same setup the redact verb exits 1 with 'cannot run git'. This output goes straight to the reviewer model in /w-fix and /w-bbs. No test covers the fallback.
fix_hint: Catch only the 'not inside a git repository' case, or none at all. For any other secretsRoots error, exit 1 and tell the user to pass --secrets-file, as the redact verb does. Add a test that runs trouble-log with git unavailable (a stubbed spawn or an empty PATH) and checks for exit 1, not unredacted output.

title: Live lock is broken at once when the holder is in another PID namespace under the same hostname
detail: deadOnThisHost decides a lock is 'this host' by hostname alone, and then calls kill(pid, 0). Containers started with --network host or --uts=host, or with the same compose hostname, share a hostname but not a PID namespace. When they share a mounted volume, the holder's pid is not visible from the waiter, so kill returns ESRCH. The waiter then judges a live, heartbeating lock stale and breaks it on its first poll. Two writers then load and save lessons.json at the same time, and the later rename drops the other's lesson or keep or retire. Confirmed: a fresh lock {host: os.hostname(), pid: 4000000, token: 'live-holder...'} is acquired over in 37 ms. A live holder should get the full staleMs wait.
fix_hint: Make the shortcut stricter: also record a boot/namespace id in the lock (for example the readlink of /proc/self/ns/pid where it exists) and apply the dead-pid shortcut only when it matches. Otherwise fall back to the unchanged-content-for-staleMs rule. Add a test with a matching hostname and a different namespace id that expects the full wait.

title: A UNC or '//' path becomes a network-path SARIF URI that resolves to a remote host
detail: fileUri turns backslashes into '/' and passes a leading empty segment through. So a finding file '\\attacker.example\share\x.js' (or '//evil.example/x.js') is emitted as artifactLocation.uri '//attacker.example/share/x.js'. Under RFC 3986 that is a network-path reference whose authority is attacker.example. Confirmed: new URL(uri, 'file:///C:/repo/').href gives 'file://attacker.example/share/x.js'. A SARIF viewer on Windows (VS Code SARIF viewer, the IDE after a code-scanning download) that resolves the location and opens it reaches out over SMB to that host, which is egress to an unexpected host and can leak NTLM credentials. f.file comes from the findings JSON, which a review agent may fill with paths taken from PR content. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/render.js:102. No test covers a UNC or '//' input.
fix_hint: In fileUri, refuse or neutralise a path that starts with '//' after backslash normalisation: either throw a KitExit for UNC/absolute non-drive paths in normalize, or drop the leading empty segments (or prefix './') so the result is always a relative path reference. Add a test that '\\\\host\\share\\x.js' and '//host/x.js' never yield a uri starting with '//'.

title: A judge's fail-closed incomplete scan, with --result given, is described as 'ran and said no' and told to pass --result again
detail: Since r4, an exit 2 from scrub (or push-gate) whose scan was cut short by a size, total or not-a-regular-file limit stays a blocking regression even with --result. That is correct, but describe/classify then return the generic regression description: 'a verb that judges the product ran and said no ... pass --result <file|-> to tell an unrun check (infrastructure) from a real verdict.' Confirmed: echo '{"hit_count":0,"not_scanned":[{"path":"a","reason":"larger than 100 bytes"}]}' | cli.js exit-codes describe 2 --verb scrub --result - prints exactly that text. Scrub found no hits; it blocked because files went unscanned (fail closed). The reader whose build turned red is told the product was judged and said no, and is told to do what they already did, with no word that the cause is an unscanned file they must shrink, split or scan with a higher limit. The description is the only explanation any surface shows, so it misleads the person trying to unblock the build.
fix_hint: When --result is given for a judge and the 2 stays blocking with hit_count 0 and a non-empty not_scanned, return a specific description (fail closed: files were not scanned for a product reason such as a size limit; it blocks; list the reasons) instead of the generic regression text; add a test that asserts the description names the unscanned reason.

title: Header still says 'complete false' or any non-empty not_scanned reclassifies scrub's 2 as infrastructure
detail: Lines 12-14 say an exit 2 is infrastructure for 'scrub with hit_count 0 and a non-empty not_scanned list or complete false', and for push-gate with 'an incomplete scan'. Since the r4 fix, incompleteNoHits (line 90) reclassifies only when every not_scanned entry has the partial-clone reason; complete false alone does nothing. Confirmed: {"hit_count":0,"complete":false,"not_scanned":[]} gives blocks true. The doc comment describes the pre-r4 rule.
fix_hint: Reword lines 12-14 to say only a zero-hit scan whose every not_scanned reason is an environment reason (partial clone) is infrastructure; size, total and other reasons stay blocking.

title: Empty piped --result says 'not valid JSON' instead of saying nothing was piped
detail: When a judge crashed or printed nothing, `judge | cli.js exit-codes blocks 2 --verb scrub --result -` gets empty stdin and fails with 'kit: --result is not valid JSON (pass the verb's JSON output)'. Confirmed with printf '' | ... (exit 1). The message suggests malformed output rather than an empty pipe, so a CI reader has to guess why.
fix_hint: Before JSON.parse, if text.trim() is empty, throw '--result is empty (the verb printed nothing; did it crash?)'.

title: Finding and ledger ids are printed raw in error messages, so control characters can rewrite the terminal and fake a line
detail: Most validation errors put the id in the message without escaping it: `finding ${id}: ...` at lines 78, 92, 96, 99 and 102, and `ledger entry ${e.id}: ...` at lines 117-119. The duplicate-id messages at lines 90 and 115 already JSON.stringify the id, so the handling is inconsistent. cli.js writes the message to stderr as it is. Finding ids come from checker output, which can be built from content in an untrusted repo. Checked: apply with id "a\u001b[31mRED\nkit: ok" and severity "bad" wrote an ANSI colour change and a second, forged line `kit: ok: severity must be ...` to the terminal. A crafted id can therefore hide or disguise the real error, or clear the screen. Raw control bytes also come through as noise in screen readers and log viewers. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/noise-ledger.js.
fix_hint: Format ids the way lines 90 and 115 do (JSON.stringify(id).slice(0, 80)) in every error message that includes a finding or ledger id.

title: --help usage leaves out --ledger/--now for accept and prune, and --in -
detail: --help returns only the `usage` string. It lists [--ledger <path>] [--now <date>] for apply only, and shows accept and prune without them, although both commands take them (header lines 5-6). It also does not say that `--in -` reads stdin. Someone who relies on --help, instead of reading the source header, cannot find out how to point accept or prune at a non-default ledger.
fix_hint: Add [--ledger <path>] [--now <date>] to accept and prune in the usage string, and note '--in - = stdin'.

title: A holder whose heartbeat stalls on a slow filesystem loses the lock, then still saves and overwrites the other run's writes
detail: withStateLock never checks that it still owns the lock before fn's write lands. If the holder's heartbeat I/O is slow (a degraded NFS/SMB link, a stalled mount, a blocked event loop), the lock content stays unchanged for staleMs, so a waiter judges it stale, breaks it and does its own load..save. The first holder then resumes and its saveState (triage.js:368/384) writes state it read before the other run, which silently drops that run's records and decisions. The header's 'parallel writers all keep their writes' does not hold, and the 'residual window' note understates this: the loss is not limited to the moment between a breaker's re-read and unlink. Confirmed with two processes, staleMs 300: holder A's heartbeat open('r+') delayed 1.5s and 1.2s of work inside the lock. B broke the lock, read 0 and wrote 1. A then wrote 1 over it. Final {count:1, by:['A']}, so B's write was lost.
fix_hint: Before the write, re-read <file>.lock and abort with KitExit 1 ('lost the lock to another run, nothing saved') when the token is no longer ours. For example, pass fn an assertHeld() and call it in visit/decide just before saveState, or do the check inside writeJsonAtomic through an option. Add a test with a slow heartbeat fs like the one above.

title: Dead-pid shortcut breaks a live lock from another machine that has the same hostname, because the pid-namespace id is the same on every Linux host
detail: The shortcut treats a lock as dead when host === os.hostname(), pidns matches and kill(pid,0) gives ESRCH. On Linux, readlink('/proc/self/ns/pid') for the initial namespace is the kernel constant 'pid:[4026531836]' (PROC_PID_INIT_INO). It is the same on every machine, and this sandbox returns exactly that. Two hosts with a default or identical hostname ('localhost', 'ubuntu', 'raspberrypi', cloned VMs or CI runners) that share the state file over a network filesystem therefore look like one host. Each sees the other's live holder pid as missing locally and breaks the lock at once, without waiting staleMs. Both then load..save and one run's triage writes are lost. Container pid-namespace inode numbers are also allocated from a small per-boot range, so they can collide across hosts too. The comment at lines 41-43 says the namespace check separates these cases, but it does not.
fix_hint: Add a per-boot machine identity to the lock, such as /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id on Linux (or a random id generated once and kept next to the state on other platforms). Apply the dead-pid shortcut only when host, boot id and pidns all match; otherwise fall back to the observation rule. Add a test where a lock has the same host and pidns but a different boot id.

title: Dead-pid shortcut trusts hostname + pidns, but the init pid namespace id is the same on every Linux machine, so a live lock from another machine with the same hostname is broken at once
detail: deadOnThisHost treats a lock as 'on this host' when lock.host === os.hostname() and lock.pidns === readlink('/proc/self/ns/pid'). The pid namespace check added in 16a4f77 does not tell machines apart: the init namespace always reads 'pid:[4026531836]' (PROC_PID_INIT_INO is a kernel constant), and this review VM reads exactly that with the generic hostname 'vm'. So two hosts that share the state folder over a network filesystem and have the same hostname (cloned VMs or CI runners, default names such as localhost/ubuntu/vm, containers given the same --hostname) look like one host. A waiter then runs kill(pid,0) against the other machine's pid, gets ESRCH and breaks the live lock immediately. Confirmed: wrote <state>.lock as {token:'other-machine', pid:3999999, host:os.hostname(), pidns:<this pidns>, beat:7} to stand for a live holder on a twin host, then ran run(['spend',...]). It removed the lock and recorded the spend in 41 ms, without waiting staleMs. Both writers then run load..save together, and the lost-update bug from round 1 comes back silently in the multi-host shared-allowance setup the round-3 fix was meant to protect. The header (state-lock.js:17-18) says clock skew 'cannot break a live lock', and that is not true here. Mirrored in .claude/helpers/kit/state-lock.js. The test at test/kit-state-lock.test.js:70 covers only a different pidns string.
fix_hint: Give each machine a real identity in the lock, for example /etc/machine-id or /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id (plus the pidns), and take the dead-pid shortcut only when that id matches. When no machine id can be read, skip the shortcut and fall back to the content-unchanged-for-staleMs rule. Add a test where a lock has the same hostname and pidns but a different machine/boot id, and assert that it waits the full staleMs.

title: Lesson text and retire reason are saved without redaction to a store that is not git-ignored
detail: trouble-log redacts project secrets, but 'lessons save' (--text, --scope) and 'lessons retire' (--reason) write the caller's strings to .claude/kit/lessons.json as given. Nothing checks them against the secrets file. The reviewer model in /w-fix and /w-bbs has the whole session in its context, not only the redacted trouble log, so it can put a credential in a lesson. That file is not in .gitignore (only .claude/kit/secrets and .claude/kit/cache/ are), so the secret can be committed, and 'lessons list' sends it back into every later reviewer prompt. Confirmed: in a repo whose .claude/kit/secrets holds 'SuperSecretToken123', `reflect lessons save --role fixer --session s1 --text "Use token SuperSecretToken123 when calling the staging API."` exits 0 and stores the token in clear. `lessons retire --id L1 --reason "token SuperSecretToken123 rotated"` also stores it, and `lessons list --all` prints both. git check-ignore reports nothing for .claude/kit/lessons.json.
fix_hint: In save and retire, load the secrets the same way trouble-log does (loadSecrets) and refuse with exit 1 when redactSecrets finds a match in text, scope or reason (or store the redacted form). Add tests for a planted secret in --text and --reason.

title: POSIX absolute paths are silently turned into a wrong repo-relative SARIF uri
detail: The new leading-segment strip in fileUri runs for every path, not just '//' UNC ones. So a single-slash absolute path, which Linux CI tools often emit (e.g. '/home/runner/work/app/app/src/x.js'), now becomes 'home/runner/work/app/app/src/x.js'. Confirmed: resolved against the checkout root, that gives file:///home/runner/work/app/app/home/runner/work/app/app/src/x.js, a file that does not exist, so the alert is attached to the wrong place. Before this commit '/home/...' was a valid absolute-path reference that resolved correctly. Drive-letter absolutes get file:///C:/... (the r3 fix), so POSIX absolutes are now handled inconsistently and wrongly. The new test pins this behaviour ('/etc/x.js' -> 'etc/x.js', '///x.js' -> 'x.js'). The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/render.js:106.
fix_hint: Strip the leading empty segments only when the path starts with '//' (UNC/network-path). For a single leading '/', emit 'file://' + the encoded path, the way drive-letter paths are handled (e.g. file:///etc/x.js). Update the test to expect file:///etc/x.js and keep the 'never starts with //' assertion for the UNC inputs.

title: push-gate deny for a tracked private pattern file is reclassified as infrastructure and stops blocking
detail: unjudgedReason treats every push-gate deny with scrub.ran false (or a reason matching /could not run/) as 'nothing was judged'. push-gate sets scrub.ran false and says 'could not run' for ANY KitExit from scrubIfConfigured (push-gate.js:258-260), and that includes scrub's product refusals: the private pattern file .claude/kit/scrub-patterns.local being tracked and about to be published (scrub.js:337), more than 200000 tracked files, and an unreadable or invalid pattern file. Confirmed: a repo with scrub-patterns.local committed; `push-gate check` exits 2 with reason 'the scrub check is configured but could not run: .claude/kit/scrub-patterns.local (the private pattern file) is tracked by git and would be published...' and scrub {ran:false}; `exit-codes classify --code 2 --verb push-gate --result pg.json` returns class infrastructure, blocks false, and tells the reader to 'Fix the environment (network, partial clone, git speed)'. CI wired to --result lets a push that publishes the private secret patterns through, and the description states a false cause. The header (lines 13-14) and REGRESSION text claim only environment failures (git timeout) take this path.
fix_hint: Reclassify a could-not-run deny only when the cause is environmental (e.g. the reason names a git timeout/overflow or 'git ... failed'); keep a refusal from scrub (private pattern file tracked, too many files, pattern file errors) blocking, or have push-gate record scrub.cause and match on it. Add a test with the private-pattern-file reason that asserts blocks true.

title: Fail-closed description gives a size remedy for reasons that are not about size
detail: The fail-closed text always ends 'Shrink or split those files, or scan with a higher limit, then rerun.' It is used for every non-environment not_scanned reason, including 'not a regular file on disk', 'tracked but missing on disk' and 'cannot read: EACCES' (scrub --worktree), where shrinking or a higher limit does nothing, and 'total size limit reached', which no flag can raise (--max-file-bytes is capped at the total), nor can push-gate check take a limit at all. Confirmed with describe 2 --verb push-gate --result - on a not_scanned of missing/not-regular files. The reasons are listed, so the reader can work it out, but the remedy is wrong for them.
fix_hint: Pick the remedy by reason (size: shrink/split or raise --max-file-bytes on scrub; total: scan a smaller range; missing/not regular/unreadable: restore or fix the file), or drop the generic remedy.

title: Empty --result from a judge's refusal is blamed on a crash
detail: scrub exits 2 with nothing on stdout when it refuses (private pattern file tracked, more than 200000 files; message on stderr). Piping that into `exit-codes blocks 2 --verb scrub --result -` fails with '--result is empty (the verb printed nothing; did it crash?)', which points the reader at a crash instead of the refusal on stderr. The header (line 23-24) also describes scrub's 2 only as 'hits or an incomplete scan', omitting these refusals.
fix_hint: Say '--result is empty (the verb printed nothing on stdout: it crashed or refused; read its stderr)' and mention scrub's refusals in the header.

title: A POSIX absolute path with three or more leading slashes becomes a wrong repo-relative SARIF uri
detail: The new POSIX branch only matches a single leading '/'. Any path starting with '///' falls through to the leading-segment strip. POSIX treats more than two leading slashes as one, so '///home/runner/x.js' means '/home/runner/x.js'. Confirmed: '/home/runner/x.js' -> 'file:///home/runner/x.js', but '///home/runner/x.js' -> 'home/runner/x.js'. Resolved against the checkout root, that second uri names a file that does not exist, so the alert lands in the wrong place. This is the same bug r5 reported, still present for this input. The new test at test/kit-sarif-junit-and-sticky-pr-comment-render.test.js:291-295 pins the wrong value ('///x.js' -> 'x.js'). Same code in .claude/helpers/kit/render.js:107.
fix_hint: Treat only exactly two leading slashes ('//' not followed by '/') as a UNC/network path. For three or more, collapse them to a single '/' and use the POSIX file:// branch, so '///x.js' -> 'file:///x.js'. Update the test expectation to match.

title: fileUri doc comment still describes only repo-relative URI references
detail: The comment says fileUri turns 'a repo path' into 'a URI reference' by converting backslashes and encoding each segment. It now also returns absolute file:/// URIs for drive-letter and POSIX absolute paths, strips leading slashes from UNC/'//' input and returns '.' for an empty result. None of that is mentioned, so a reader who trusts the comment will misread how locations are produced. Same in .claude/helpers/kit/render.js:98.
fix_hint: Reword the comment to list the cases: drive-letter and single-'/' absolute paths -> file:/// URI; leading '//' or UNC -> leading slashes stripped, relative; otherwise a relative reference; empty -> '.'.

title: push-gate's truncated not_scanned list hides an oversized unscanned file, so a fail-closed deny is reclassified as infrastructure
detail: unjudgedReason calls incompleteNoHits(result.scrub) on push-gate's result, but push-gate keeps only the first 20 not_scanned entries (push-gate.js:263, r.not_scanned.slice(0, 20)) and scrub lists the partial-clone 'object not available locally' entries first (scrub.js:335), before any 'larger than' or 'total size limit reached' entries. With more than 20 missing objects plus one oversized file, push-gate's list shows only partial-clone reasons. Confirmed: blob:none clone of a repo with 25 small files and a 34 MB big.bin containing AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP (pattern AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}), big.bin fetched, remote then made unreachable. `scrub` exits 2 with 26 not_scanned (last: big.bin 'larger than 33554432 bytes') and `exit-codes blocks 2 --verb scrub --result scrub.json` gives blocks true; but `push-gate check` exits 2 with scrub.not_scanned of 20 partial-clone entries, and `exit-codes classify --code 2 --verb push-gate --result pg.json` returns class infrastructure, blocks false, 'skipped files only for an environment reason'. CI wired to --result lets a push carrying an unscanned secret-bearing file through.
fix_hint: Have push-gate record the full not_scanned count (or the set of distinct reasons) in its result and reclassify only when that count equals the listed length and every reason is environmental; or treat a push-gate not_scanned list of 20 (possibly truncated) as not reclassifiable. Add a test with 21+ partial-clone entries followed by a 'larger than' entry asserting blocks true.

title: --result - buffers all of stdin before applying the 1 MiB cap
detail: readResult reads the whole of stdin via io.stdin() (cli.js readStdinBytes concatenates every chunk, then toString copies it) and only then checks Buffer.byteLength against MAX_RESULT_BYTES. The documented 1 MiB limit therefore bounds nothing in memory. Confirmed: piping 400 MB into `cli.js exit-codes blocks 2 --verb scrub --result -` reaches maxRSS of about 1218 MB before failing with '--result is larger than 1048576 bytes' (about 56 MB for a normal input). Piping the wrong command's output (a diff, a log, a binary) into a CI step can exhaust a runner's memory instead of failing fast with the clear error.
fix_hint: Read stdin incrementally (for await over the stream, or a bounded reader passed in io) and throw the 'larger than' error as soon as the running byte total passes MAX_RESULT_BYTES; add a test with a stdin larger than the cap that asserts the error without buffering it all.

title: Element text, including any secret in it, is stored in plain text in a state file that git does not ignore
detail: visit stores each candidate's normalised element signature verbatim in rec.members (line 256), and saveState writes it to the default .claude/kit/triage.json. Normalisation only lower-cases the text and masks pure hex runs of 8+ and digit runs of 4+, so mixed tokens survive. That path is not in .gitignore (only .claude/kit/secrets is), so a commit of the working tree publishes it. triage list also prints the members. Confirmed: a violation with element 'AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE secret=hunter2pass' leaves "members": ["akiaiosfodnn7example secret=hunter2pass"] in triage.json. Findings from security checks (a hardcoded credential, a token in a page) often carry the offending text as their element. The suite's redact verb exists for exactly this, but triage never uses it.
fix_hint: Store members as hashes, e.g. sha256 of the normalised signature (matching only needs equality), and keep readable labels out of the state; also add .claude/kit/triage.json* to .gitignore. Add a test asserting that a raw element string never appears in the saved state.

title: The default state path follows a repo-controlled symlink and writes outside the working tree
detail: stateFile() resolves .claude/kit/triage.json against cwd. withStateLock (state-lock.js:157,165) and writeJsonAtomic (state-lock.js:248-267) then mkdir, create the lock and temp file, and rename through plain paths, so a .claude/kit committed as a symlink sends every write to wherever it points. Confirmed: with repo/.claude/kit -> ../../outside, a plain `triage visit` created outside/triage.json (and its lock and temp file) outside the repo. A tracked or reviewed repo can therefore make the verb create triage.json* in any folder the user can write to, or overwrite another project's triage ledger. The suite already routes writes of this kind through guarded-fs (review-score, push-gate) to refuse this. Impact is limited to files named triage.json*, so this is graded medium, not high.
fix_hint: For the default path (no explicit --state), resolve and write through guarded-fs with root = cwd (or the git toplevel) so a link inside .claude/kit is refused, or at least lstat .claude, .claude/kit and the state file and refuse a symlink. Add a test with .claude/kit as a symlink that leads outside the root.

title: triage list shows only opaque hashes, so records on one scope+rule cannot be told apart
detail: Members are now sha256 hex (candidatesOf line 205), and list (line 415) prints them as the only per-record detail. Confirmed: after visits flagging 'button.submit' and then 'a.forgot-link' for login/contrast, list shows two records with the same scope and rule whose members are just 64-char hashes. A user who decides later from list, not straight from the visit report, cannot tell which fingerprint is which element. The header (line 21, 'stored with the set of element signatures') and the usage still describe readable signatures.
fix_hint: Say in usage and the header that list members are hashes and that the readable `elements` come only in the visit report. Optionally keep a short redacted label per member (passed through the redact verb's scrubbing) so list can show it without storing raw text.

title: Exit code 2 from the new symlink refusal is not in triage's usage or header
detail: guardDefaultState (line 155) exits 2 ('kit: refused: ...'), confirmed with .claude/kit linked out of the tree. But the triage usage string (line 54, 'exit 0 done, 1 invalid input or corrupt state') and the header (line 42) list only 0 and 1. The kit-wide convention in cli.js defines 2 as a policy refusal, so the meaning is recoverable, but the verb's own help is wrong.
fix_hint: Add '2 refused: the default state path goes through a symbolic link' to the usage string and the header's exit codes.

title: Library entry fails open: a mistyped verb or an unparsed result makes a judge's exit 2 stop blocking
detail: The header (line 15) names classify()/blocksMerge() as the library input method, and the brief says code integrations call a module function. That path skips the checks the CLI path makes. (1) classify() never validates the verb, unlike toVerb() on the CLI: blocksMerge(2, 'Scrub') and blocksMerge(2, 'scrub ') return false, and classify({code:2, verb:'pushgate'}) returns class precondition. The CLI rejects these with exit 1. (2) blocksMerge wraps classify in try { } catch { return false }, so an input error becomes 'does not block'. Passing the judge's stdout string as given, which is the natural call after spawnSync (blocksMerge(r.status, 'scrub', r.signal, r.stdout)), returns false even when that output has hit_count 3. With no result, the same 2 blocks (true). Confirmed: blocksMerge(2,'scrub',null,'{"hit_count":3,"not_scanned":[]}') returns false, while blocksMerge(2,'scrub',null,{hit_count:3,not_scanned:[]}) returns true. On this input method, a mistake by the integrator turns a real regression (a secret hit or a push-gate deny) into a green gate with no error. The CLI fails closed on the same mistakes. The test at test/kit-exit-code-contract-separating-infrastruc.test.js:83 only checks that a bad code returns false. It does not cover a bad result or a bad verb for a judge.
fix_hint: In classify, reject a verb outside the registered set (or at least one that is a case or whitespace variant of a PRODUCT_JUDGES name) with KitExit 1. In blocksMerge, rethrow input errors, or return true when code === 2 and the verb is a product judge, so bad input never unblocks a verdict. Add tests for blocksMerge(2,'scrub',null,'<json string>') and blocksMerge(2,'Scrub') that assert they do not return false silently.

title: shared-budget has no --help; asking for help is an error
detail: parse() rejects every flag outside VALUE_FLAGS, so `cli.js shared-budget --help` and `cli.js shared-budget grant --help` print 'kit: unknown flag --help' and exit 1. Sibling verbs (caller-floor.js:216/253, diff-range.js:85/204, graph.js:1331) accept --help/-h and return { usage }, and their errors end with '(see --help)'. A user who follows that suite convention gets an error and no per-verb usage. The only way to see the usage is the global `cli.js help` dump. The error messages also do not point there. Confirmed by running both commands. Mirrored in .claude/helpers/kit/shared-budget.js.
fix_hint: In parse(), treat --help/-h as a boolean that makes run() return { usage } before the --state check, and add '(see cli.js shared-budget --help)' to the unknown-flag and missing-command errors.

title: Numeric flags reject valid numbers with 'must be a number'
detail: num() accepts only /^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/. `--cost .5` prints 'kit: --cost must be a number', and so does `--steps 1e3`. Both values are numbers, so the message misleads the user about what went wrong. Confirmed on the CLI. Mirrored in .claude/helpers/kit/shared-budget.js.
fix_hint: Either accept what Number() parses as finite (the later limitOf/nonNeg checks already enforce positive and integer), or reword the error to give the accepted form, e.g. '--cost must be a plain decimal such as 0.5'.

title: Corrupt-state error does not name the file
detail: checkState throws 'budget state is corrupt' without the path. The missing-file and invalid-JSON errors in load() (lines 304-305) do include the resolved path. With several jobs' state files, the user cannot tell from the message which file to inspect or delete. Confirmed: `status --state c.json` with {"version":2} prints only 'kit: budget state is corrupt'.
fix_hint: In load(), catch the checkState KitExit and rethrow it as `budget state ${file} is corrupt`.

title: accept/prune change the committed ledger's file mode to 0600
detail: writeJsonAtomic creates its temp file with mode 0o600 and renames it over the target, so after any accept or prune the committed .claude/kit/noise-ledger.json becomes owner-read-only, whatever the umask or the file's previous mode. Before the state-lock adoption (6ffb2c2) the ledger was written with fs.writeFile (umask, 0644 under 022), so this is a regression. Checked: a 0644 ledger became -rw------- after `cli.js noise-ledger accept --id a --reason r --ledger l.json`. Git does not record the change, so nobody notices, but on a shared checkout or a bind-mounted repo read by another uid (a CI container, a teammate's account) every later apply/accept/prune fails with 'cannot read ...: EACCES' (exit 1), breaking the advisory step. The header documents nothing about modes. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/state-lock.js.
fix_hint: Keep the target's existing mode: stat the file before writing (fall back to 0o666 & ~umask when it does not exist) and chmod the temp file to it before the rename; add a test that a 0644 ledger stays 0644 after accept.

title: Exit-code doc says 1 means invalid input or broken ledger only
detail: The header says 'Exit codes: 0 done (findings or not), 1 invalid input or broken ledger' and the usage says '1 for invalid input', but exit 1 is also returned when the ledger is locked by another run past waitMs, when the lock is lost before the rename ('nothing saved'), and when the ledger or its folder cannot be written (EACCES/EROFS). A caller reading the docs would treat a lock timeout as a bad-input problem.
fix_hint: Say '1 invalid input, broken ledger, or the ledger could not be locked or written' in the header and usage.

title: Header's fingerprint formula no longer matches the code
detail: Lines 20-21 say the fingerprint is the first 16 hex of sha256 over scope, rule and the sorted unique element signatures. Since d13d8a5, candidatesOf (line 205) puts sha256(signature) into c.sigs, so line 266 hashes over the sorted signature hashes. Confirmed: for scope p, rule r1, element a.x the documented formula (fingerprintOf('p','r1',['a.x'])) gives 8a45714d2b426541, but visit records 77b0abf2f1861aba. A caller or tracker that rebuilds or checks a fingerprint from the header (fingerprintOf is exported) gets a different value. The fingerprint of the same finding also changed between ledgers written before and after this commit, and the header does not say so.
fix_hint: Change the header to 'sha256 over scope, rule and the sorted unique sha256 hex of each element signature', and say that members are those hashes. Also say that fingerprints from ledgers written before d13d8a5 differ, while matching still goes by member overlap after migration.

title: Migration test passes even with the migration removed
detail: 'a plain-text ledger from before is migrated to hashes and still matches' builds r1 with the new code, so its fingerprint is already the hashed one. It then sets members to plain text and checks only that r2's fingerprint equals r1's and that '"a.x"' is gone. Without the migration line (triage.js:144) nothing overlaps, so a new record is created under the same key, fingerprintOf over the same hashed sigs. It overwrites the old record, and both assertions still pass. Confirmed by calling visit() on a ledger with plain members and no migration: same fingerprint, raised with status 'new', and a record that was 'filed' with issue '#12' becomes status 'new' with issue null. That is the decision and issue loss the migration exists to prevent, and nothing guards it. A real pre-d13d8a5 ledger also has fingerprints over plain signatures, which this test never builds.
fix_hint: In the test, mark the record filed with an issue (or build the record under a fingerprint computed over plain signatures, as the old code did). Then assert that r2 reports it in recurred with that issue, status pending/filed and not 'new', and that the record count stays at 1.

title: Exit code 2 (symlink refusal) still missing from header and usage
detail: guardDefaultState (line 155) exits 2, but the header (line 46) and the usage string (line 59) still list only '0 done, 1 invalid input or corrupt state'. r5 reported this at the same commit and it is unchanged.
fix_hint: Add '2 refused: the default state path goes through a symbolic link' to both.

title: Header and usage still describe members as readable element signatures
detail: Members are now 64-hex sha256 values (lines 144 and 205), and list (line 416) prints them as the only per-record detail. Line 21 ('stored with the set of element signatures (its members)') and the usage do not say that members are hashes, or that readable elements appear only in the visit report. r5 reported this and it is unchanged.
fix_hint: Say in the header and usage that members are sha256 hashes of the signatures and that readable `elements` appear only in the visit report.

title: Migration comment overstates: plain-text members stay on disk after list
detail: The comment says that hashing old members means they 'no longer sit on disk'. The hashing happens in loadState in memory, and only visit and decide save. A user who runs only `triage list` on an old ledger keeps the plain-text element signatures, which may hold secrets, in .claude/kit/triage.json until the next write.
fix_hint: Reword to 'are replaced on disk at the next visit or decide', or save the migrated state, under the lock, when loadState changed any member.

title: A judge's empty or partial output makes exit-codes fail on the infrastructure outcomes it exists to classify
detail: The result is parsed before the signal and the status are looked at. In classify, line 162 parses a string result before the signal check at line 163. In the CLI, readResult runs for every code (lines 268 and 275). The result only matters for a judge's exit 2, but a crashed, killed or timed-out judge prints nothing or truncated JSON, and then the whole call throws KitExit 1 instead of returning infrastructure or usage. Confirmed with an empty out.json: `exit-codes classify --signal SIGKILL --verb scrub --result out.json`, `classify --code 137 ...` and `blocks 124 --verb scrub --result out.json` each exit 1 with '--result is empty'. A truncated push-gate output with 124 exits 1 with 'not valid JSON'. In the library, blocksMerge(null,'scrub','SIGKILL','') and blocksMerge(127,'scrub',null,'') throw. CI that always passes the judge's output (the documented way to tell an unrun check from a verdict) gets an error, and a red step under set -e, for exactly the crash, signal, timeout(1) and not-found cases the contract says must never turn a build red. The same applies to a judge's empty-stdout refusal (exit 2), which should classify as a blocking regression rather than as bad input. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/exit-codes.js.
fix_hint: Parse or read the result only when code === 2, the verb is in PRODUCT_JUDGES and there is no signal. For a judge's 2 with empty output, return regression with blocks true and a 'printed nothing (refusal or crash); read stderr' description instead of throwing. Add tests for signal, 124, 127 and 1 with an empty or truncated result, through both the CLI and blocksMerge.

title: A status that contradicts the result's own exit field is trusted, so a scrub with hits can be classified clean
detail: Every judge result carries the status it exited with (scrub always has "exit", and push-gate has exit 2 on a deny), but classify never compares it with the code it was given. The --result - form makes a mismatch likely: in `judge | cli.js exit-codes blocks <code> --verb scrub --result -` the judge's status cannot reach the right-hand side, so callers hard-code 2 or pass a stale $?. Confirmed: `echo '{"hit_count":3,"exit":2}' | cli.js exit-codes blocks 0 --verb scrub --result -` returns class clean, blocks false, so a secret hit passes the gate when $? was 0 from the previous command. In the other direction, a real clean scrub (exit 0) piped into `blocks 2 --verb scrub --result -` returns regression, blocks true, a false red. Both are error paths with wrong input that the result itself could catch, and neither one fails.
fix_hint: When a result is given and has a numeric exit field, throw KitExit 1 if it differs from the code (or use result.exit when no code is supplied). Add tests for 0-with-exit-2 and 2-with-exit-0.

title: Lessons in any language whose first letter is not plain ASCII are refused with a misleading 'starts with a verb' error
detail: checkLessonText requires /^[A-Za-z]/ on the text, and line 232 strips every non-ASCII letter from the first word. A lesson written in German, French, Russian, Japanese and so on is refused with exit 1 and 'a lesson starts with a verb (imperative)', even when it does start with an imperative verb. Confirmed through cli.js in a fresh git repo: 'Éteignez le cache avant les tests.', 'Überprüfe die Konfiguration vor dem Deploy.', 'Проверьте конфигурацию перед деплоем.' and '設定を確認してからデプロイする。' all exit 1 with that message, while 'Run the linter before pushing changes.' saves. A team or reviewer model working in another language cannot save any lesson, and the error tells it to fix something that is not wrong. The same ASCII-only rule in words() (line 205, /[^a-z0-9\s]/) splits accented words into fragments ('Vérifiez' becomes 'v' and 'rifiez'), so the near-match guard scores non-English lessons on broken word pieces.
fix_hint: Use Unicode letter classes: test /^\p{L}/u on the text, strip with /[^\p{L}']/gu for the first word, and normalise words() with /[^\p{L}\p{N}\s]/gu; add a test that saves a lesson starting with an accented capital and one in a non-Latin script.

title: A large partial-clone scrub result (the degraded-network case) is classified as a blocking regression
detail: scrub's not_scanned list has no cap (scrub.js:335 adds one entry per missing object), and cli.js prints it pretty-printed at about 160 bytes per entry. A zero-hit scrub in a sparse or partial clone with the remote unreachable and about 6,600 or more missing files therefore prints more than MAX_RESULT_BYTES (1 MiB). The header names this exact case as infrastructure that never blocks. This diff now treats an oversized result at exit 2 as 'Fail closed ... the judge crashed or refused' and returns blocks: true (judgeResult line 110, readResult lines 156/163). Confirmed: a 1.1 MB scrub result with 7,000 entries, all reading 'object not available locally (partial clone?)', with hit_count 0 and exit 2, gives `exit-codes classify --code 2 --verb scrub --result big.json` -> class regression, blocks true. The same result with 6,000 entries -> infrastructure. The library is inconsistent with itself: classify({code:2,verb:'scrub',result:obj}) returns infrastructure, but blocksMerge(2,'scrub',null,<the same text>) returns true. So a monorepo whose network is degraded gets a false red gate. The description also misleads: the judge did not crash, and 'rerun it' will not help.
fix_hint: Cap scrub's not_scanned output (keep a count plus the first N entries and a flag saying whether every reason is an environment reason) so a judge's own result always fits under the cap. Alternatively, raise or remove the size cap for a file --result, and make the string and object library paths apply the same rule. Add a test with a zero-hit partial-clone result larger than 1 MiB.

title: words() still splits words at combining marks, so decomposed accents and Indic scripts are scored as fragments
detail: The new class /[^\p{L}\p{N}\s]/gu keeps letters but not combining marks (\p{M}). An accented word typed in decomposed (NFD) form, which macOS input and some tools produce, still breaks apart: words('Vérifiez la configuration'.normalize('NFD')) gives ['ve','rifiez','la','configuration']. overlap() of that text with the same text in NFC is 0.4, below the default threshold of 0.5, so an exact duplicate lesson passes the near-match guard and is saved again. Scripts whose vowel signs are combining marks break up even in NFC: words('परीक्षण से पहले कैश जाँचें') gives ['पर','क','षण','स','पहल','श','ज','च']. This is the same fragmenting that r5 reported and the test name says is fixed ('scores accented words whole'), and it still applies to these inputs. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/reflect.js:205.
fix_hint: Normalise with String(text).normalize('NFC') before lowercasing, and keep marks in the class: /[^\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}\s]/gu. Add an NFD-vs-NFC duplicate case and a Devanagari case to the test.

title: Japanese and Chinese lessons, now accepted, get no protection from the near-match guard
detail: The diff starts accepting lessons in scripts that do not put spaces between words (the test saves '設定を確認してからデプロイする。'). words() splits only on whitespace, so a whole CJK sentence becomes one token: words('設定を確認してからデプロイする。') is ['設定を確認してからデプロイする']. Two lessons that differ by a single character score an overlap of 0. For example, overlap('設定を確認してからデプロイする。','設定を確認してからデプロイしてください。') is 0. So near-duplicates are always saved as new lessons, and the 'confirm by id rather than duplicate' rule in the brief does nothing for these languages.
fix_hint: For runs of Han, Hiragana, Katakana or Thai (\p{Script=Han} etc.), emit character bigrams instead of one token, and add a test that two near-identical Japanese lessons trip the near match.

title: The one-sentence rule ignores full-width sentence ends, so multi-sentence CJK lessons pass
detail: The ONE-sentence check matches only /[.!?]\s+\S/. Now that CJK lessons are accepted, checkLessonText('設定を確認する。デプロイしてからログを見る。') returns the text unchanged even though it holds two sentences. The Russian 'Проверьте конфиг! Потом деплой.' is refused as expected.
fix_hint: Also treat 。！？ followed by any non-space character as a sentence break, e.g. /[.!?]\s+\S|[。！？]\s*\S/.

title: The imperative check is English-only, so non-English lessons that are not imperative are accepted
detail: checkLessonText now admits any script, but NON_IMPERATIVE_START lists only English articles and pronouns. 'Die Konfiguration ist kaputt.' and 'Le cache est cassé.' are both accepted, although they are statements and not imperatives. The validator's promise that 'a lesson is imperative' is therefore enforced only for English text.
fix_hint: Add the common German, French, Spanish and Russian articles and pronouns to the list, or say in the help and error text that the imperative check applies only to English.

title: A secret in a file outside a sparse partial clone passes the gate: the 'partial clone' skip is treated as a network fault, but scrub never fetches
detail: ENV_REASONS treats 'object not available locally (partial clone?)' as an environment reason, and the header (line 13) and NOT_JUDGED (line 89) justify this as 'a partial clone with the remote unreachable'. But safe-git always sets GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 (safe-git.js:199), so scrub never fetches a missing blob, whether or not the remote can be reached. In a sparse, blobless clone (git clone --filter=blob:none --sparse, common for monorepo CI), every file outside the sparse cone is always skipped with this reason. The network is fine and a rerun gives the same result. Scrub correctly fails closed (exit 2, complete:false), but exit-codes turns that into class infrastructure, blocks:false. Confirmed locally with no network: a repo with other/leak.txt containing an AKIA key and a matching pattern in .claude/kit/scrub-patterns, cloned via file:// with --filter=blob:none --sparse. `cli.js scrub` gives exit 2, hit_count 0, and both files in not_scanned with that reason. Then `cli.js exit-codes blocks 2 --verb scrub --result out.json` gives {class:'infrastructure', blocks:false}. A CI job that follows the contract (fail only when blocks is true) goes green on a commit carrying a secret that was never scanned. The push-gate path at line 110 does the same for lists under 20 entries. The description also misleads: 'Fix the environment (network, ...) and rerun' cannot help. This is a security boundary (the secrets gate) failing open on a deterministic, repo-shaped condition, not on a transient infrastructure fault.
fix_hint: Do not reclassify the missing-object reason as infrastructure. It is a scan that cannot run in this clone configuration, so keep it blocking (fail closed) with a remedy such as 'fetch the missing blobs (git fetch / unsparse) or run in a full clone'. If you keep a non-blocking path, gate it on evidence that a fetch was attempted and failed. Add a test with a sparse blobless clone whose skipped file holds a hit pattern, and assert blocks is true.

title: Comment says the temp file always starts at 0600; for a new file it starts at 0666 & ~umask
detail: The new comment reads 'The temp file starts at 0600 and takes the target's mode before any content is written.' Line 261 opens the temp file at 0600 only when the target exists. When the target is missing it opens at 0o666, so under umask 022 the temp file is 0644 (world-readable) from creation. That is the same mode the final file gets, so nothing is exposed that would not be exposed anyway. But a reader auditing temp-file privacy would take the comment to mean the temp is always private. The same text is in .claude/helpers/kit/state-lock.js:255.
fix_hint: Reword: 'For an existing target the temp file starts at 0600 and takes the target's mode before any content is written; for a new one it is created at 0666 & ~umask.' Make the change in both copies.

title: A full-width sentence end followed by a closing quote or bracket is read as a second sentence
detail: The new full-width rule /[。！？｡]\s*\S/ counts any non-space character after 。！？ as the start of another sentence, including closing punctuation. A single quoted Japanese sentence such as checkLessonText('「設定を確認してからデプロイする。」') is refused with 'a lesson is ONE sentence', although it holds one sentence. Placing 。 inside 」 or ） is ordinary Japanese style. The English branch does not have this problem because it requires whitespace after [.!?]. The same line is in .claude/helpers/kit/reflect.js:248. No performance or memory problem was found: with 20,000 stored lessons a save takes about 0.3 s, and words() on a 200,000-character input takes about 40 ms.
fix_hint: Skip closing punctuation before testing for a following character, e.g. /[。！？｡][」』）〕】"'\)\]]*\s*[^\s」』）〕】"'\)\]]/u, and add the quoted-sentence case to the text-handling test table.

title: The text promises the unscanned files, but the description never names a file
detail: The regression description that users see at runtime (line 47) says 'Pass --result <file|-> ... for the hit count, the unscanned files with reasons and a remedy'. The header (line 14) also says --result describes 'the unscanned files with their reasons'. But describeJudge (lines 118-124) only prints a count and the distinct reasons. It never prints a path. Confirmed: describe 2 --verb scrub --result - with not_scanned [{path:'other/leak.txt',...},{path:'big.bin',...}] returns '2 file(s) were not scanned (object not available locally (partial clone?); larger than 1048576 bytes)' and no file names. A reader who follows the advice to learn which files blocked the gate gets no file names. They have to dig through the raw JSON, which is what the description was supposed to save them from. The same text is in .claude/helpers/kit/exit-codes.js.
fix_hint: Add the first few not_scanned paths, with a '+N more' count, to the description. Or change the wording at lines 14 and 47 to 'the number of unscanned files and their reasons'.

title: -h is not taken as help, and 'describe -h' gives a misleading error
detail: run() only knows --help. 'exit-codes -h' exits 1 with 'unknown subcommand "-h"'. 'exit-codes describe -h' exits 1 with '<code> must be an integer 0..255, got "-h"', which does not tell the user that help exists. Sibling kit verbs (graph.js:1331, impact.js:360, caller-floor.js:216) accept -h, so a user who learned the kit's short help flag gets an error here.
fix_hint: Treat '-h' the same as '--help' in both checks at lines 297-298.

title: Missing-blob remedy says 'git fetch', which does not get the missing blobs back
detail: For the reason 'object not available locally (partial clone?)' the description tells the user 'Fetch the missing blobs (git fetch, or unsparse the checkout) or run in a full clone'. In a blobless or sparse partial clone, the clone keeps its filter, so a plain `git fetch` only fetches new refs and never fills in blobs that are already missing. Confirmed locally (file:// clone with --filter=blob:none --sparse, then `git fetch origin`): `git rev-list --objects --missing=print HEAD` shows the same missing blob before and after the fetch. A user who follows the first remedy and reruns scrub gets the same fail-closed exit 2. The description itself says 'a rerun in the same clone gives the same result', so the user is left confused about why the advice did not work. The same text is in .claude/helpers/kit/exit-codes.js:116.
fix_hint: Drop 'git fetch' from the parenthesis, or replace it with a command that does fetch the missing blobs (e.g. 'git sparse-checkout disable', or 'git backfill' on git 2.49+).

title: diff-range exit 1 description leaves out the 'skipped by a cap' case its usage text names
detail: diff-range's usage text (diff-range.js:83) says exit 1 covers 'bad input or git failed or files skipped by a cap left the diff empty', and diff-range.js:350 throws KitExit 1 for that case. The override description only says 'Bad input, or git failed or timed out while diff-range ran'. So a range that is empty only because untracked files went over --max-file-bytes or --max-untracked is described as a malformed call or a git failure, even though the fix is to raise a cap. 'read the message' softens this, but the description is meant to give the same text on every surface. Same in .claude/helpers/kit/exit-codes.js:72.
fix_hint: Add ', or untracked files skipped by a cap (--max-file-bytes/--max-untracked) left the diff empty' to the diff-range 1 description.

title: Missing-blob remedy suggests plain 'git backfill', which skips the missing blobs in a sparse checkout
detail: scrub only reports 'object not available locally (partial clone?)' for HEAD's tree (scrub.js:176-187 via ls-tree; history mode exits 1 instead). In a blobless clone HEAD's blobs inside the checkout are already present, so the missing ones are the paths outside a sparse-checkout cone. Per git-backfill's documentation (git 2.49+), '--sparse is assumed' when sparse-checkout is enabled (builtin/backfill.c sets sparse from core_apply_sparse_checkout), so a plain 'git backfill' downloads only blobs at paths inside the cone and leaves exactly the blobs scrub needs missing; the rerun gives the same fail-closed exit 2 the text was changed to avoid. Not reproduced locally (this machine has git 2.43, without backfill); based on git's documented default. Same text in .claude/helpers/kit/exit-codes.js:116. The test at test/kit-exit-code-contract-separating-infrastruc.test.js:558 accepts 'backfill' alone, so it would not catch this.
fix_hint: Say 'git backfill --no-sparse on git 2.49+' (or keep only 'git sparse-checkout disable'), and have the r13 test match the exact command.

title: Missing-blob remedy now offers only 'git sparse-checkout disable', which does nothing in a non-sparse blobless --no-checkout clone
detail: Confirmed locally (git 2.43, file:// promisor remote, no network): 'git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout' (no --sparse) then 'kit scrub' exits 2 with every HEAD file reported as 'object not available locally (partial clone?)'. Running the remedy's only named command, 'git sparse-checkout disable', returns 0 but fetches nothing (there is no index or checkout to widen), and scrub rerun gives the same exit 2. The text also frames the problem as blobs 'outside the sparse cone', which is not the case here. The r15 change dropped 'git backfill', which in a non-sparse clone does fetch all blobs, so this error path lost its only working fetch command; only 'or run in a full clone' remains. Same text in .claude/helpers/kit/exit-codes.js:116.
fix_hint: Name the non-sparse case too, e.g. '(git sparse-checkout disable in a sparse checkout, git checkout in a --no-checkout clone, or git backfill --no-sparse on git 2.49+; a plain git fetch does not fill them in)', and keep the test matching the exact commands.

title: Missing-blob remedy now names no command at all, and lists clone shapes that do not cause missing blobs alone
detail: After r16 the scrub missing-blob remedy says 'Fetch the missing blobs (the command depends on how the clone was made: sparse, --no-checkout or blobless; ...)' but gives no command for any of those shapes. A user on an older git (2.43 here, no backfill) is told what not to run but not what to run, which is the case this angle covers. diff-range does give a concrete command for the same condition (diff-range.js:144). Also, 'sparse' and '--no-checkout' do not leave blobs missing by themselves; only a filtered (blobless) clone does, so listing them as three alternatives misleads. A single command works on every git version and clone shape: confirmed locally (git 2.43, file:// promisor remote, no network) that in a 'git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout' clone, 'git archive HEAD >/dev/null' takes HEAD's missing blobs from 2 to 0. Because this is only remedy text and the exit code is unchanged, it is low. Same text in .claude/helpers/kit/exit-codes.js:116.
fix_hint: Name one version-independent command, e.g. 'Fetch the missing blobs once (git archive HEAD >/dev/null works on any git version and clone shape; a plain git fetch does not fill them in) or run in a full clone', and make the r13 test match it exactly.

title: CI 'npm test' step goes green on a broken test script (127), any exit 2, and any status >= 128
detail: runStep treats every 'precondition' or 'infrastructure' class as exit 0. classify() was built for kit verbs, so with no verb it maps 2 to the kit's non-blocking 'refusal' (precondition), 126/127 to precondition, and 124 or >= 128 to infrastructure. 'npm test' is not a kit verb. Confirmed: a package.json whose test script names a missing binary (e.g. 'nodee --test ...') makes npm exit 127 and the step exits 0. CI_TEST_COMMAND='exit 2' and 'exit 137' also exit 0. The job therefore passes with zero tests run when the test script is broken, when the runner is OOM-killed (137) or aborts (134), and for any runner that reports failures as 2 (mocha counts failures, tsc type errors). A '::warning::' annotation is the only signal, and 'Show failing tests' (if: failure()) no longer runs. The 'Exit code contract' row is blocking, so this is a finish-line check that is not enforced. test/reach/ci-job.test.js:93 asserts that 127 stays green, which locks the bug in.
fix_hint: Fail closed for an external test command: let only a signal or 124 be advisory, and only after a retry also hits infrastructure; otherwise fail. At minimum treat 2, 126, 127 and 128+ as failures: 'npm test' with exit 127 means no test ran, not that the product is fine. Change the 127 reach case to expect a failure.

title: Advisory steps sit after the actions they must precede and after the section's AUTO-PROCEED handoff
detail: The w-review NOISE LEDGER AND TRIAGE block says 'Before any candidate is filed' but comes after CHECKPOINT 4's '4. Add entry to .claude/ralph-candidates.md', its REQUIRED OUTPUT and 'AUTO-PROCEED: Continue to Verification phase.' The same happens with the w-review CLUSTER block (line 2548, 'before the list is shown', after CP1's REQUIRED OUTPUT and AUTO-PROCEED), the w-bg-review Phase 4 CLUSTER block (line 2859, 'before candidates are listed', after the candidates are written and after AUTO-PROCEED) and the w-fix TEST PLAN block (line 1676, after 'AUTO-PROCEED: Continue to Verification'). The blocking w-fix AUTO-FIX GATE (line 1723) sits after the Verification section's 'PASS -> proceed to next phase' and its closing '---'. An agent following the workflow top-down has already filed or listed the findings, or has been told to move on, before it reaches these steps. The reach test passes only because stepSection reads to the next ### heading, not because the step runs at the right point.
fix_hint: Put each block before the REQUIRED OUTPUT / AUTO-PROCEED lines of its section (the noise ledger before step 4 'Add entry'). Put the AUTO-FIX GATE before RETRY LOGIC inside the Verification section. Regenerate the command files, and have the reach test assert that the step comes before the section's AUTO-PROCEED line.

title: noise-ledger reach call always fails with exit 1, and the test accepts it
detail: The call passes '--ledger <tmp>/ledger.json', a file that never exists. noise-ledger apply then exits 1 ('ledger.json does not exist'; confirmed). The assertion allows [0, 1], so the reach proof for the noise-ledger power passes on an invalid-input error. It would also pass if the verb were broken. This test is the evidence that 'wired --record' and delivered.md use for that power.
fix_hint: Drop --ledger (the step does not pass it), or create the ledger first. Assert exit 0 and check the output (for example, 'filed' holds id 'a').

title: check prints a fix that names a command the CLI does not have
detail: When the kit helper is missing, check now exits 4 and prints 'fix: Install the suite in this project: run danizee-claude-suite install.' (text from doctor.js:189). The CLI has no 'install' command, only init, update and install-user. A project installed by an older suite version is reported as installed but has no kit, so this wrong fix is the only remedy shown, and following it gives 'unknown command'.
fix_hint: Change the fix to 'run npx danizee-claude-suite init (or update for an existing install)'.

title: w-fix TEST PLAN describes $C as the changed paths, but --changed takes a file
detail: The step says '$C lists the changed paths one per line (git diff --name-only)', so C=$(git diff --name-only) is the natural reading. test-plan's usage is '--changed <file>', and passing the list itself gives 'cannot read changed list ... ENOENT' with exit 1 (confirmed). The step then falls back to 'run the full suite', so the power never takes effect when the text is followed literally.
fix_hint: Say '$C is a file holding the changed paths, one per line (git diff --name-only > "$C")', the way $M is described.

title: Marathon helper allowance uses one fixed state file that later runs inherit
detail: 4.1a opens the allowance at .claude/marathon/helper-budget.json 'once per stream (skip when the file exists)'. The path is not scoped to the run id or the stream, and nothing removes the file when a run ends. The next /w-marathon in the same repo skips 'open' and grants from the old state. Confirmed: after a run that used its steps, 'grant' returns {skip:true, reason:'steps limit exhausted'} with exit 0. The step treats that as 'the allowance is used up: do not spawn, go to CHECKPOINT 5', so every later marathon stops at its first spawn. Re-running 'open' does not help, because it exits 1 ('already exists'), which the step reads as broken state. A second stream of the same run also skips 'open' and shares the first stream's allowance, which contradicts 'covers all helper sessions of the stream'.
fix_hint: Scope the state to the run (and stream), e.g. .claude/marathon/<run-id>/helper-budget-<stream>.json, and open it in step 4.2 when the stream is activated.

title: A grant with no amount reserves the whole allowance, so a concurrent spawn or a dead helper stops the run
detail: 'shared-budget grant --helper <id>' without --steps/--parts reserves everything that is available (grantFor: divisor 1 returns avail). Confirmed: after h1's grant, h2's grant returns skip:true 'steps and cost limit fully reserved by other sub-sessions'. Streams run in parallel, so the second concurrent builder or reviewer gets skip. The step then reads skip as 'used up' and goes to CHECKPOINT 5, ending the run while the allowance is unspent. The text never says to 'release' a helper that dies without spending, so its reservation stays for good. The 'spend' call is also printed without --state; run as written, it exits 1 ('--state <file> is required') and the reservation is never settled.
fix_hint: Pass --steps/--cost (or --parts <live helpers>) on grant, add --state to the spend line, add 'shared-budget release --state <f> --helper <id>' for a helper that ends without a spend, and treat a 'fully reserved' skip as 'wait', not as 'used up'.

title: w-review claim budget opens a fixed file once, so every later review stops claim checks
detail: Step 1 runs 'shared-budget open --state .claude/kit/review-budget.json --steps 30' once per review. The file is never removed or scoped to the review. On the second /w-review in a project, 'open' exits 1 (confirmed: 'b.json already exists'). The text maps exit 1 to 'broken state, report it and start no more sub-sessions', so no claim-checking sub-session runs again after the first review. If the open error is ignored, grants come from the first review's spent state and return skip:true ('steps limit exhausted').
fix_hint: Use a per-review state path (e.g. include the PR number or session id), or remove the file at the end of the checkpoint; treat 'already exists' on open as a stale file to replace, not as broken state.

title: Blocking replay gate in w-review lets the check pass on invalid input or a missing kit
detail: The row 'repeated replay gate → /w-review VERIFICATION' is blocking, and the run decided that judges fail closed. Here, exit 1 (invalid or unreadable $G, e.g. a typo in the file path: confirmed exit 1 'cannot read ... ENOENT') maps to 'nothing fails the check on unreplayed evidence'. Line 2616 says the same when the kit is missing. In both cases a replayed, reproducing failure that the gate would block (exit 2) is reported as passing, and the Verification checkpoint reaches 'PASS -> proceed'. A gate that cannot run gives the most permissive result. In w-debug, by contrast, the same exit 1 leaves the diagnosis unconfirmed.
fix_hint: On exit 1 or a missing kit, mark the check as unresolved (FAIL with 'replay gate could not run'), fix $G and rerun, or ask the user; never let it count as PASS.

title: Reach tests, including the CI fail-closed proof, are not run by npm test or CI
detail: package.json 'test' is 'node --test test/*.test.js', which does not match test/reach/*.test.js. scripts/ci-step.js testTargets also lists only test/*.test.js. The CI job's 'npm test' therefore never runs ci-job.test.js (fail closed on 2/124/127/137/signal), cli-check.test.js (check exit 0/1/4) or workflows-bugpatrol.test.js (each step comes before its handoff). A change that makes runStep fail open again, or a regeneration that moves a step after AUTO-PROCEED, passes CI. The only thing that runs these tests is 'bbs wired', by hand.
fix_hint: Change the test script to 'node --test test/*.test.js test/reach/*.test.js' (and let testTargets read test/reach too).

title: Helper allowance clock is never stopped after an interrupted lead session, so a resumed marathon ends at its first spawn
detail: 4.1a wraps each helper in 'shared-budget start' / 'stop', and 4.2 says that on a resumed stream 'already exists' means keep the file. If the lead session dies, is compacted or restarts (precompact/SessionStart hooks and the launchd/crontab fallback wake exist for exactly this) between start and stop, the state keeps depth >= 1 and clockRunning: true. Nothing in the text says to inspect or stop it on resume. The downtime is then counted, and every later start/stop pair leaves depth at 1 or more, so the clock never stops. Confirmed with --now: open --time-ms 3600000, start at 0, a resumed start at 7200000 and a stop give depth 1, clockRunning true, elapsedMs 7300000; the next grant returns {skip:true, reason:'time limit exhausted'} with exit 0. The step reads that as 'the allowance is used up: do not spawn, go to CHECKPOINT 5', so the stream stops after a crash with its steps and cost unspent.
fix_hint: On resume (and before the first grant of a session), run 'shared-budget status --state "$S"' and issue 'stop' until depth is 0. Better: do not count wall-clock across sessions; either drop --time-ms from the marathon allowance or record time per helper (from the task notification) through spend.

title: w-review claim budget keeps its path in shell variables across separate Bash calls, so the per-review state degrades to /review-budget.json
detail: The step says to run D=$(mktemp -d) 'at the start of this checkpoint', use B="$D/review-budget.json" for open/grant/spend/release around each sub-session, and run rm -rf "$D" at the end. Those calls are separate Bash tool calls with sub-sessions between them. Claude Code does not keep shell variables between calls, so D is empty in the later calls and B becomes '/review-budget.json'. As a normal user, open fails (EACCES, exit 1), which the text maps to 'broken state, start no more sub-sessions', so no claim is checked. As root (containers, CI), a fixed file at the filesystem root is created; rm -rf "" removes nothing, and Claude Code's own safety check refuses an rm -rf on an empty or unresolvable variable. The next review's open then exits 1 'already exists', which is the cross-run leak that r2 asked to remove.
fix_hint: Have the step print the path (D=$(mktemp -d) && echo "$D") and tell the agent to use that literal path in every later call and in the final rm. Alternatively use a deterministic per-review path such as .claude/kit/review-budget-<session id>.json, removed with a guarded [ -n "$D" ] && rm -rf "$D".

title: check skips the project's doctor checks and passes a broken doctor config
detail: check calls runDoctor({profile, cwd, env}) without loading .claude/kit/doctor.json. The doctor verb's run() loads that file. As a result, a project check marked fatal is never run by 'danizee-claude-suite check'. Confirmed: with doctor.json requiring env MY_REQUIRED_KEY (fatal), 'kit/cli.js doctor' exits 2 and 'check' exits 0. With an invalid doctor.json ('{bad'), the doctor verb exits 1 and check still exits 0. The row 'Preflight doctor checks -> cli check' is blocking, and scripts or CI that read check's exit code get 'clean' for a project whose own fatal prerequisite is missing, or whose config is broken.
fix_hint: Use the doctor's run() entry (or load the config the same way: loadConfig(cwd, findProjectRoot(cwd)) and pass custom/customBase) so check honours .claude/kit/doctor.json; map its KitExit 1 to the usage code. Add a reach case with a fatal project check that expects exit 4.

title: Exit 2 from the test command is labelled 'the test command could not start'
detail: classify() with no verb maps 2 to precondition, and runStep prints 'precondition: the test command could not start' for it. Several runners use 2 for failing tests or type errors (mocha counts failures, tsc, pytest), and node itself exits 9 or 1 for bad flags, not 2. The step still fails correctly, but the ::error:: annotation points the reader at setup instead of at failing tests.
fix_hint: For an unknown status that is not 126/127, use a neutral label (for example 'test command failed with status N'). Keep 'could not start' for 126/127 and spawn errors.

title: cli-check reach test needs Node 20.6+ but the package claims node >=20.0.0
detail: The test starts node with '--import <register.mjs>', and register.mjs calls module.register(). Both arrived in Node 20.6.0. package.json engines is '>=20.0.0', and npm test now runs test/reach/*.test.js. On Node 20.0-20.5 every check case fails with a bad-option error, not a product failure. CI uses the latest 20.x, so it does not see this.
fix_hint: Raise engines to >=20.6.0, or skip the shim when the real dependencies resolve (spawn without --import when commander can be imported).

title: Reflection steps put model-written lesson text inside a double-quoted shell argument, so backticks and $( ) in a lesson run as commands
detail: The w-fix REFLECTION step (line 1730) and the w-bbs Reflection step (line 5206) tell the agent to save each lesson with `reflect lessons save ... --text "<lesson>"` (and to retire one with `--reason "<why>"`). The lesson is written from the trouble log: failed commands, error text and test output, which can come from the code under review. Inside double quotes bash runs backticks and $( ). Lessons usually name commands in markdown backticks. Confirmed: `reflect lessons save --role fixer --text "Run `touch INJECTED; echo npm ci` before the tests" --session s1` created the file INJECTED and stored 'Run npm ci before the tests'. So a lesson such as 'Run `git stash` first' or 'Run `npm ci` before tests' runs that command while it is saved, and an error message that holds $(...) can run it too. The suite's own search step (line 84) forbids this pattern: 'never into a double-quoted shell argument ... backticks and $( ) in an error message would run as commands'.
fix_hint: Have the agent write the lesson with the Write tool to a temp file outside the repo, and pass it so it is not shell-evaluated: add `--text-file <f>` to reflect lessons save (and `--reason-file` to retire), or at least say to use a single-quoted argument with ' escaped. Apply the change to both the w-fix and w-bbs steps, then regenerate the command files.

title: w-review posts the rendered PR comment without redacting project secrets, and writes the reports into an unignored reports/ folder
detail: RENDER REPORTS tells the agent to 'post the comment yourself' from reports/review-comment.md. render never redacts. Confirmed: with .claude/kit/secrets listing sk_live_ABCDEF123456, a finding 'Hardcoded key sk_live_ABCDEF123456 in .env' is copied verbatim into the comment markdown. Security findings often quote the value they found, including values from git-ignored files such as .env that are not in the PR. Posting the comment sends the secret to GitHub, where everyone who can see the PR can read it. The suite's other text that leaves the machine (the search steps at lines 84-101) goes through `redact` first. The same files are also written to reports/ at the repo root, which .gitignore does not cover, so a later 'commit all changes' can commit them.
fix_hint: Pipe the comment (and the SARIF/JUnit) through `node .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js redact --keep-lines` before it is posted or kept, and refuse to post when redact fails. Write the outputs to a mktemp directory, or add reports/ to .gitignore.

title: CI ::error:: annotation for a failing test run says 'never block on it' next to 'The job fails'
detail: runStep appends classify()'s description, which was written for kit verbs, to the one annotation a reader sees on a red job. For the ordinary case (npm test exits 1 because tests failed), the confirmed output is: '::error::"npm test" ended with status 1: product failure: tests failed. Invalid input, broken state, or a tool failure (not separable yet): the call was malformed or the data unusable, or the tool crashed or a git child failed, since cli.js reports any crash as 1. Check the message before blaming the caller; never block on it. The job fails.' For status 2 it says 'The verb refused the call ... Nothing was judged about the product, so it never blocks; change the call or the environment ... The job fails.' For status 3 it talks about safe-git and diff-range. The label and the description contradict each other, and the description sends the person to arguments, verbs and cli.js instead of to the failing tests. This shows on every failing CI run.
fix_hint: Do not append c.description for the test command; end the line with the label and one concrete next step (for example 'see Show failing tests' for a product failure, 'rerun' for infrastructure, 'check the test script / node install' for 126/127).

title: check on a mistyped --path exits 4 (missing prerequisite) and tells the user to run init there
detail: check never checks that --path exists. 'check --path /nonexistent/x' (confirmed) lists 'file:.claude/helpers/kit/cli.js ... not found (looked in /nonexistent/x)' with the fix 'run npx danizee-claude-suite init', prints 'Fatal: ...' and exits 4. With --profile marathon it prints four fatal checks and four fixes (init, create marathon.json, git init), none of which help. A typo in the argument is a usage error, and the help text promises '1 usage, 4 a fatal prerequisite is missing'. A script or CI step that reads the exit code is told a prerequisite is missing, and a person is sent to install into a directory that does not exist.
fix_hint:
Before the status and doctor run, stat options.path; if it is missing or not a directory, print 'check: --path

does not exist (or is not a directory)' and exit checkExitCode(1). Add a reach case for it.

title: noise-ledger and triage are chained with && but the exit codes are explained per verb, and errors do not say which verb failed
detail: The w-review NOISE LEDGER step runs 'noise-ledger apply ... && triage visit ...' as one command and then explains exit 0/1 for noise-ledger and exit 0/1/2 for triage separately. The agent sees one combined status. Both verbs print errors as 'kit: cannot read ...' (confirmed), with no verb name. When the status is 1, it cannot tell which instruction applies. When noise-ledger fails, triage silently does not run, and nothing in the text says that.
fix_hint: Run the two verbs as two separate commands (or two lines that each echo their own exit, e.g. 'echo "noise-ledger exit $?"'), so each exit code maps to its own paragraph.

title: CI 'Render test results' writes JUnit/SARIF into $RUNNER_TEMP and nothing ever uploads or comments them
detail: The integration row for 'SARIF JUnit and sticky PR comment renderers' on job node-test says the report 'is uploaded and commented' on pull requests. The step calls reportStep, which writes junit.xml and results.sarif under resultsDir() = $RUNNER_TEMP/test-results (scripts/ci-step.js:13).
