No later step uploads them (no actions/upload-artifact, no SARIF upload, no PR comment), and GitHub wipes RUNNER_TEMP when the job ends. The only trace is the log line 'wrote /home/runner/work/_temp/test-results/junit.xml', which points at a file nobody can open. The reach test only checks that the files exist on local disk, so it passes. The step's own comment ('nothing is posted') is accurate. But the power recorded as delivered on this surface gives the user nothing to read.
fix_hint: Add an 'if: always()' actions/upload-artifact@v4 step for $RUNNER_TEMP/test-results (per matrix node version), or write the files somewhere a later step publishes. Otherwise change the row and delivered text so they say the job only prints a summary.

title: w-review triage step names a path that does not exist: kit/cli.js triage decide
detail: The step says to record a decision with `kit/cli.js triage decide <fingerprint> --as ...`. Every other command in the workflow uses node .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js. From the project root there is no kit/cli.js (confirmed), so the line fails as written. A decision that is never recorded means filed candidates are never marked decided. The same text is in the installed .claude/commands/.shortcuts/w-review.md:162.
fix_hint: Write `node .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js triage decide <fingerprint> --as filed|dismissed|accepted [--issue <ref>]` and regenerate the command files.

title: Any test-command status that classify calls infrastructure (e.g. 5) is labelled 'timed out / killed by a signal, rerun'
detail: classify() with no verb maps 5 to infrastructure, so runStep labels a plain exit 5 'infrastructure: timed out / killed by a signal, rerun ... rerun the job'. Confirmed: CI_TEST_COMMAND='exit 5' prints that annotation. Runners that use 5 for an ordinary result (pytest: no tests collected, among others) are told to rerun a job that will fail the same way. The job still fails correctly, so only the label is wrong.
fix_hint: Say 'timed out / killed by a signal' only for 124, codes >= 128 or a signal. Label other statuses with the neutral 'test command failed with status N'.

title: Noise-ledger input schema leaves out its severity values, and 'critical' is rejected
detail: The step gives $F as {"id","severity",...} with no allowed values. The CLUSTER step a few lines earlier takes critical|high|medium|low|info, and w-review's reviewers commonly grade 'critical'. noise-ledger accepts only high|medium|low. Confirmed: a 'critical' finding gives exit 1 'severity must be high, medium or low'. The step then skips both the ledger and triage and files candidates as before, so one critical finding switches the power off for the whole review.
fix_hint: State 'severity: high|medium|low (map critical to high, info to low)' in the $F description and regenerate the command files.

title: /mt 4.5 triage: `recurred` and `closed` can never appear, so recurred rows are never marked
detail: 4.5 says to write every row with source "agent" and never runs `triage decide`. In triage.js an undecided record seen again comes back in `raise` with status `pending`, not in `recurred` (only `filed` records recur), and a record with any agent-sourced violation never closes on absence (`skipped`, agent_sourced). I ran it: six visits on one state file (r1 to r6) gave `recurred: []` and `closed: []` every time, the repeated row came back as `raise` `pending`, and the vanished one as `skipped` `agent_sourced`. So 'note `recurred` entries (seen in an earlier round)' and 'mark recurred ones' in the 4.7 fix brief never happen, and the step does not deliver what it claims. /pt CHECKPOINT 6 (line 1003) has the same `closed` claim for agent findings.
fix_hint: In 4.5, read repeats from `raise` entries with status `pending` (or `reopened`) as the recurred rows, and say that `closed` stays empty for agent-sourced rows. Otherwise run `triage decide <fp> --as filed` after a row is recorded so it recurs.

title: Replay-gate input does not give the run shape, so natural input fails /pt Verification (and /mt line 4958 never closes a finding)
detail: /pt and /mt write `"runs":[run1,run2]` and never say what a run is. replay-gate accepts only objects with steps/checks/outputs and rejects anything else with exit 1: I ran `runs:["exit 1","exit 1"]` and got 'runs[0] must be an object' (rc 1), and `runs:[{"exit":1},{"exit":1}]` got 'unknown key "exit"' (rc 1). In /pt, exit 1 makes Verification FAIL ('replay gate could not run'). In /mt 4.7, no finding in the file is closed that round. So the normal flow fails closed for a format reason, not a real block. /w-debug (line 1947) does spell out `{"steps":[...],"outputs":{...}}`.
fix_hint: Spell out the run shape in both steps, as /w-debug does, e.g. `"runs":[{"steps":[...],"checks":{...},"outputs":{...}}, ...]` (at least one key, no other keys).

title: /pt router step does not list the valid answer kinds, so a guessed kind routes every claim to ask-human
detail: route.json is described as `{"answer":{"kind","confidence"}}` with no allowed values. threshold-route accepts only anomaly|not-anomalous|ambiguous|suppress|fix|check. I ran kind "concern" and it came back `ask-human` / malformed-answer, and kinds a model would likely write for the claims the step names ("tests pass", "auto-fix") do the same. Result: the user is asked about every claim and no fix is ever routed `auto-fix`. This fails safe, which is why it is low. /mt (line 4953) does give `"kind":"fix"`.
fix_hint: List the kinds in the /pt step (fix for a fix claim, suppress for a suppression, check for 'tests pass').

title: /mt 4.5 cluster: 'id the row's index' invites a numeric id, which cluster rejects
detail: cluster requires a non-empty string id. I ran `{"id":0,...}` and got 'finding #1: "id" must be a non-empty string', exit 1. The step tells the writer to use the row's index, so a JSON number is the natural choice, and then the rows stay unclustered every round. This is advisory, so nothing is lost but the grouping.
fix_hint: Say `"id":"<row index as a string>"`, e.g. "0".

title: test-map hand-written by the model every /mt fix round (and in /pt) although CI derives it mechanically
detail: 4.7 check 1 (and the /pt CHECKPOINT 5 step, line 916) has the model write a full `{targets:[{id,files}]}` map for the repo. In /mt this repeats every round, because the temp directory is removed after each round. This repo has about 110 test files, so that is thousands of tokens per round. A partial or hand-guessed map drops below min-mapped-pct and falls back to the smoke set, which leaves the step with little effect. scripts/ci-step.js already builds the targets mechanically (testTargets) for the same verb.
fix_hint: Generate the map from the same helper CI uses (or keep one map per run outside the per-round temp directory) instead of having the model write it.

title: /pt reflection never says where the session event log is
detail: The block needs 'the literal path of the session's event log (JSON Lines)', but nothing in /pt creates such a log or names where one is (the Claude Code transcript under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl, which trouble-log accepts). A model that cannot find it gets exit 1 ('cannot read events'), so the advisory reflection usually yields nothing.
fix_hint: Name the transcript location (or the generic schema to write) in the step.

title: /mt fix check 1 builds the test map once from the main checkout, so it never has the stream's own tests and the plan is the smoke set
detail: Check 1 says to generate .claude/marathon/<run-id>/test-map.json once per run from the main checkout with `node scripts/ci-step.js --print-targets`. But the fixer works on the stream's worktree, and testTargets() only lists test files that exist in the directory it runs in. I ran it that way: with the map built from the main checkout, the changed files src/lib/kit/cluster.js, doctor.js and replay-gate.js mapped to nothing ('only 0 of 3 changed files (0%) map to a target'), and the plan was the 3 alphabetical smoke tests (agent-browser-workflows, autoresearch-workflow, bbs-cli). The same changed files with the map built in the worktree gave the 3 matching kit tests as direct-change. A stream that adds code and tests, which is the normal case, therefore always gets an unrelated smoke plan. One map per run is also shared by every stream, although each worktree has different tests. In this run the main checkout has no scripts/ci-step.js at all, so the step falls back to the hand-written map that round 7 meant to remove.
fix_hint: Generate the map in the stream's worktree, once per stream, e.g. `(cd <worktree> && node scripts/ci-step.js --print-targets) > .claude/marathon/<run-id>/test-map-<stream>.json`, and say to regenerate it when the stream adds a test.

title: /mt 4.5 cluster input (rule = category, files = file) marks distinct findings as duplicates of one defect
detail: cluster's pass 1 puts findings with the same rule and the same file set in one bucket, with no title or line check. 4.5 maps rule to the row's category (one of 9 coarse values) and files to its single file. Then it tells the lead that 'duplicates of one defect go to the fixer together'. I ran it on round 7's real rows: four unrelated correctness findings on src/plugins/dot-shortcuts.js (triage repeats, replay-gate run shape, router kinds, cluster id) came back as one cluster [0,1,2,3], with no pending pair to judge. Reviewer rows often share a category and a file, so in the normal flow the fix brief tells the fixer that separate defects are one defect, and one fix can be claimed for all of them. /pt CHECKPOINT 6 (line 989) leaves rule undefined and invites the same coarse mapping.
fix_hint: Make rule specific to the defect, e.g. `"rule":"<category>: <title>"`, so that only matching rows bucket together. Or stop calling a cluster 'duplicates' in the brief and call it 'same category and file'.

title: Saved lessons are never read back, so keep/retire of 'a listed lesson' cannot be done and lessons never reach a later run
detail: The /pt reflection (like /w-fix line 1775 and /w-bbs line 5298) saves lessons and then says '`reflect lessons keep --id <id>` confirms a listed lesson that held; `retire --id <id>` drops one that no longer does'. No step in any workflow runs `reflect lessons list` or loads .claude/kit/lessons.json (grep finds no 'lessons list' in src/plugins), so the model has no ids to keep or retire. The lessons also never feed a future session, which defeats the power's purpose ('saved lessons for future runs'). The role is also left as `<role>`: near-duplicate detection only compares lessons of the same role, so a role chosen differently on each run saves duplicates freely. I confirmed that save, the near-duplicate refusal (exit 2 with the id) and --confirm work when called with a fixed role.
fix_hint: Name a fixed role per workflow (e.g. `--role pt`). Add a step that runs `reflect lessons list --role <that role>`, both at the start of the workflow (to apply the lessons) and before the save (to keep or retire by id).

title: /pt cluster input does not say id is a string; a numeric id makes cluster exit 1
detail: Round 7 fixed this in /mt (line 4900) but not in /pt: findings.json is `[{"id","rule","severity","files":[...]}]` with no type for id. Findings from parallel agents have no ids of their own, so a model numbers them. I ran `{"id":0,...}` and got 'finding #1: "id" must be a non-empty string', exit 1, so the findings stay unclustered.
fix_hint: Say `"id":"<a string, e.g. \"f1\">"` as /mt now does.

title: /pt router step tells the model to use kind `check` for 'tests pass' but never explains the `issue` and `ignore` routes that come back
detail: I ran the step as written. A `check` claim with no regression always comes back `issue` ('a model-only check has no deterministic backing'), whatever its confidence. A high-confidence `anomaly` also comes back `issue`, and `not-anomalous` comes back `ignore`. 'Act on each route' lists only suppress, auto-fix, ask-human, escalate and block, so the most common answer to the claim the step names ('tests pass') is a route the model has no instruction for.
fix_hint: Add: `issue` means raise it as a finding (a 'tests pass' claim is not accepted on a model's word: the re-run decides); `ignore` means drop it.

title: Generated test map leaves out every test that reaches code by spawn or path.join, so changes to bin/cli.js or scripts/ci-step.js map to no test
detail: testTargets() only picks up static `../` imports. The reach tests start bin/cli.js and scripts/ci-step.js with spawnSync or `import(path.join(...))`, so the map /pt and /mt now generate does not link them. With changed.txt holding src/lib/kit/doctor.js and bin/cli.js, test-plan reported bin/cli.js as unmapped, went low_confidence, and planned 3 unrelated smoke tests instead of test/reach/cli-check.test.js. On this stream's last two commits only 3 of 9 changed files were mapped, and scripts/ci-step.js was unmapped although ci-job.test.js tests it. The plan is advisory, so it only orders the work.
fix_hint: Also take path strings that test files pass to spawn or path.join (e.g. 'bin/cli.js', 'scripts', 'ci-step.js') as dependencies in testTargets().

title: /pt and /mt test-map generator exists only in the suite repo; in an installed project it is missing, or an unrelated scripts/ci-step.js gets run
detail: /pt CHECKPOINT 5 (line 922) and /mt fix check 1 (line 4960) build the map with `node scripts/ci-step.js --print-targets`. That file lives only in this repository's scripts/. The installer does not ship it, and nothing outside dot-shortcuts.js references ci-step, so .claude/helpers/kit has no equivalent. In every installed project the step therefore falls back to the hand-written map that round 7 removed, although the text says 'never by hand'. The `[ ! -f .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js ]` guard does not cover the generator. A project that has its own scripts/ci-step.js, a common name for a CI script, gets that unrelated script run with an unknown flag (whatever its default action is, such as a deploy or publish step), and its stdout is redirected into test-map.json, where test-plan then rejects it with exit 1.
fix_hint: Ship the map builder (testTargets/spawnedPaths) as a kit verb, e.g. `node .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js test-plan --scan` or `kit/cli.js test-map`, and call it through the existing kit-missing guard instead of scripts/ci-step.js.

title: Lessons read back are applied as 'standing instructions' with no limit, so a saved lesson can switch off a mandatory gate in later runs
detail: The new CHECKPOINT 0 blocks in /pt (761), /w-fix (1627) and /w-bbs (5167) say to 'apply each listed lesson to this run as a standing instruction'. Lessons are model-written from a trouble log, and that log is mostly failed actions and repeated calls. The natural lesson from a check that kept failing is to skip or loosen it (e.g. 'Skip the scrub step when fetched files exceed the size cap'), and reflect's validation only checks for one imperative sentence of 12..200 characters. The store .claude/kit/lessons.json is tracked in git (not in .gitignore), so a committed lesson also reaches every collaborator's runs. In /w-bbs the trouble log comes from auditing an untrusted fetched source. The read-back gives the stored text instruction authority over the workflow's own MANDATORY and blocking steps.
fix_hint: Say the lessons are advice that never overrides a step, gate, exit-code rule or safety rule of this workflow, and that a command named in a lesson is never run because the lesson says so. Keep the 'standing instruction' wording out.

title: /mt per-stream map: a failed or empty generation is kept for the whole stream and makes test-plan exit 1 every round
detail: `(cd <worktree> && node scripts/ci-step.js --print-targets) > .claude/marathon/<run-id>/test-map-<stream>.json` truncates the target before node runs. If the worktree has no scripts/ci-step.js, node exits 1 with MODULE_NOT_FOUND and a 0-byte map is left behind (confirmed). If the worktree has no test/*.test.js or test/reach/*.test.js, the generator exits 0 with {"targets":[]} (confirmed). test-plan rejects both with exit 1 ('input is not valid JSON' / '"targets" must be a non-empty list'). The map is built 'once per stream' and only regenerated when a test file is added, so every later round repeats the same exit 1, which the step reads as 'invalid input, the fixer runs the full suite'. Nothing tells the lead to check the generator's exit status or the map's size.
fix_hint: Write to a temp file and move it into place only when node exits 0 and targets is non-empty. Otherwise delete it and fall back as described.

title: Lessons read-back has no recovery for a broken or merged store; a duplicate id makes one lesson impossible to retire
detail: The store is tracked in git, and nextId is max+1 per branch, so two branches that each save a lesson both create the same id, or a merge conflict leaves conflict markers. With conflict markers or invalid JSON, `reflect lessons list` exits 1 at CHECKPOINT 0 and again before the save, and every save and keep exits 1 too. The steps only say 'Exit 1: invalid input, report it', so the power stays off on every later run. With a clean merge, list shows two lessons with id L1. I ran this: `retire --id L1` retires only the first one, and a second retire gives 'lesson L1 is already retired', exit 1. So the 'take an id from that output' rule cannot reach the second lesson. A store holding {"lessons":[null]} exits 1 with 'Cannot read properties of null'.
fix_hint: On exit 1 from lessons list, say to name the store path and tell the user to repair or move .claude/kit/lessons.json. Make the kit refuse or renumber duplicate ids when it loads the store.

title: /w-fix TEST PLAN runs on unset $M and $C, with no way given to build the map
detail: The /w-fix CHECKPOINT 2 block runs `test-plan --in "$M" --changed "$C"`, but nothing in /w-fix sets M or C. Shell variables do not carry over between Bash calls, and unlike /pt (line 922) this block never says to run `mktemp -d`, never says to build the map with `test-plan --scan`, and uses no literal paths. With M empty, `--in ""` is parsed as no --in, so the verb reads stdin. Confirmed: `node .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js test-plan --in "$M" --changed <file> </dev/null` prints 'input is not valid JSON' and exits 1. In a real /w-fix run this row cannot produce a plan: it always falls through to 'run the full suite', so the wired power never takes effect. Also, `git diff --name-only` leaves out the new untracked files a fix creates.
fix_hint: Use the same pattern as /pt: run `mktemp -d` once, generate `<dir>/test-map.json` with `test-plan --scan`, write changed.txt from `git diff --name-only HEAD` plus untracked files, and put literal `P=<dir>` paths in the block, with the same scan-failed/empty-map fallback.

title: /w-fix and /w-bbs reflection read an unset $E, so no fixer/bbs lesson is ever saved for the new read-back
detail: The REFLECTION blocks of /w-fix (line 1783) and /w-bbs (line 5312) run `reflect trouble-log --in "$E"`. They describe $E only as 'the session's event log': no command sets it and no path is given. /pt was fixed to use a literal E= path and to point at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl. With E unset, `--in ""` reads empty stdin. Confirmed: this exits 1 with 'the input has no events'. So the trouble-log row never yields signals in these two workflows. The `reflect lessons list --role fixer` and `--role bbs` read-backs added at intake in this diff will therefore always list nothing.
fix_hint: Reuse the /pt wording in both blocks: a literal `E=<path>` example and the instruction to substitute the newest transcript under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/.

title: Changed paths are git-root relative but the scanned map is cwd relative: projects in a subfolder of a repo never map
detail: /pt writes changed.txt with `git diff --name-only HEAD`, and /mt (line 4960) uses `git -C <worktree> diff --name-only <base>`. Both print paths relative to the git top level. `test-plan --scan` writes ids and files relative to the current directory. When the project is a subfolder of a larger repo (a monorepo package, or a project inside a dotfiles repo), no changed path ever matches the map. Every plan is then 0% mapped, low_confidence, and a smoke set only. Confirmed: in a repo with app/src/a.js and app/test/a.test.js, running from app/ gives unmapped ['app/src/a.js'] and a plan with only the reason 'smoke'. The advice to 'add each new untracked file' makes it worse: `git ls-files --others` prints cwd-relative paths, so the list mixes both bases.
fix_hint: Use `git diff --name-only --relative HEAD` (in /mt, run it from inside the worktree or the project subfolder) so the paths share the scan's base, and `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` for untracked files.

title: Reflection now reads the full Claude transcript, but only .env values are redacted before a lesson is committed
detail: This diff points the REFLECTION blocks of /pt (line 1081), /w-fix (1783) and /w-bbs (5312) at the whole session transcript (~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl). That transcript holds every tool input and output, including credentials that are not project secrets: a token from `gh auth token`, an Authorization header in a curl command, an env var. `reflect trouble-log` and the `lessons save` guard (src/lib/kit/reflect.js:427-433) redact only exact values from the project's secrets files. The blocks tell the model that a lesson 'can quote an error message', and the store .claude/kit/lessons.json is not git-ignored and is read back into later prompts. Confirmed in a scratch repo: a failed Bash event whose error holds ghp_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789 comes out of trouble-log unredacted ('failed: Bash - curl: (22) 401 token ghp_... bad'). `lessons save --text-file` with that token then exits 0 and writes it verbatim into lessons.json.
fix_hint: Before save, and on trouble-log output, also reject or mask credential-shaped strings (ghp_/github_pat_/sk-/AKIA/xox*/Bearer <token>/long high-entropy runs). Or add .claude/kit/lessons.json to .gitignore and tell the blocks never to quote tokens.

title: Blocking gates hard-code a real-looking shared /tmp path (/tmp/tmp.AbC123)
detail: The literal-path rewrite replaced $R/$G placeholders with runnable defaults: R=/tmp/tmp.AbC123/route.json in the /w-fix AUTO-FIX GATE and G=/tmp/tmp.AbC123/gate.json in the /w-debug REPLAY GATE (line 1961). The /pt and /mt blocks do the same, with 33 uses in all. The name matches mktemp's own pattern and sits in world-writable /tmp. If the model runs a block verbatim (it is valid shell), it reads whatever is at that fixed path rather than failing on an unset variable. A file planted there by another local user would decide the auto-fix route or the replay gate, and the `> "$P/test-map.json"` redirect would follow a planted symlink. Usually the missing directory makes the block fail closed, so this needs both a model slip and a shared host.
fix_hint: Use a non-runnable placeholder such as P='<printed dir>' (or :"${P:?set P to the mktemp -d output}"), so a block run without substitution fails instead of using a fixed shared path.
